conversation.user: Compare Civil Technology certificate and associate certificate.
conversation.advisor:
## Civil Technology: Certificate vs. Associate Certificate

| Feature | Civil Technology Certificate | Civil Technology Associate Certificate |
|---|---|---|
| Credential | Certificate | Associate Certificate |
| Study mode | Part-time | Part-time |
| Delivery/campus | Blended; Burnaby Campus / Online | Blended; Burnaby Campus / Online |
| Program status | Listed as active | Active |
| Verified credit requirement | Not available from the retrieved program details | Minimum **30.0 credits** |
| Curriculum | Certificate requirements could not be verified from the available Asteris data | Includes required-course alternatives plus **at least 9.5 credits from an approved elective pool** |
| Flexibility | Details unavailable | Courses can be selected to suit the student’s needs; approved Associate Certificate courses may be incorporated into Certificate requirements |
| Current notice | Details unavailable | The program is under review and a curriculum change is planned |

### Key difference

The **Associate Certificate** is a flexible, part-time credential requiring a minimum of **30.0 credits**. The specific requirements and credit total for the **Certificate** could not be verified from the available program record, so I can’t reliably state how many additional courses or credits it requires.

The Associate Certificate record also states that it is **not available to international applicants** and that Program Declarations require Civil Engineering department approval.

- [Civil Technology Certificate](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-certificate-part-time-5430cert/)
- [Civil Technology Associate Certificate](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-associate-certificate-part-time-5430acert/)

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.

It is **not available to international students**. It is a **part-time, blended** program delivered through the **Burnaby Campus / Online**, requiring a minimum of **30.0 credits**.

Program details:  
https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-associate-certificate-part-time-5430acert/

If you mean **international students**, no—the **Civil Technology Associate Certificate** is **not available to international applicants**.

For eligible applicants, admission is on a **first-qualified basis while space remains**, subject to the entrance requirements. See the program details:  
https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-associate-certificate-part-time-5430acert/

Please note that this program is not available to international applicants. International applicants interested in civil technology are encouraged to view the BCIT Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering . Delivery: blended. See details . The Part-time Associate Certificate in Civil Technology is designed to provide students and employers a flexible offering of academic courses to advance careers in the field of Civil Technology. A program of study can be tailored to a student’s needs by selecting appropriate courses from the list of electives. An Associate Certificate must contain a minimum of 30.0 credits and approved courses from the Associate Certificate can be incorporated into the requirements for a Certificate . How to Apply There is no formal application process and it is not necessary to register in the program to take courses. You may register for any course of interest as long as the specified prerequisite(s) are met or you have the equivalent knowledge. Students who wish to complete the Associate Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* January 2nd* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* April 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* September 1st* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Recommended for success Math: one of the following (or equivalent): Math 12* or MATH 0001 – Technical Mathematics *Students who completed Math 12 more than five years ago are strongly recommended to start with one of the required math courses. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Program declaration Declaring your Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) program ensures that BCIT is aware of your intent to complete a program as it is currently outlined and provides you the opportunity to apply for transfer credit. To submit your declaration: Answer all questions completely. If required, convert transcripts and documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Declare Now Upon approval, a program plan letter will be sent to you confirming your program of study. Please allow approximately eight weeks for processing. Learn more about program declaration Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

content.text:
## Civil Technology: Certificate vs. Associate Certificate

| Feature | Civil Technology Certificate | Civil Technology Associate Certificate |
|---|---|---|
| Credential | Certificate | Associate Certificate |
| Study mode | Part-time | Part-time |
| Delivery/campus | Blended; Burnaby Campus / Online | Blended; Burnaby Campus / Online |
| Program status | Listed as active | Active |
| Verified credit requirement | Not available from the retrieved program details | Minimum **30.0 credits** |
| Curriculum | Certificate requirements could not be verified from the available Asteris data | Includes required-course alternatives plus **at least 9.5 credits from an approved elective pool** |
| Flexibility | Details unavailable | Courses can be selected to suit the student’s needs; approved Associate Certificate courses may be incorporated into Certificate requirements |
| Current notice | Details unavailable | The program is under review and a curriculum change is planned |

### Key difference

The **Associate Certificate** is a flexible, part-time credential requiring a minimum of **30.0 credits**. The specific requirements and credit total for the **Certificate** could not be verified from the available program record, so I can’t reliably state how many additional courses or credits it requires.

The Associate Certificate record also states that it is **not available to international applicants** and that Program Declarations require Civil Engineering department approval.

- [Civil Technology Certificate](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-certificate-part-time-5430cert/)
- [Civil Technology Associate Certificate](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-technology-associate-certificate-part-time-5430acert/)

conditions.description: How to Apply There is no formal application process and it is not necessary to register in the program to take courses. You may register for any course of interest as long as the specified prerequisite(s) are met or you have the equivalent knowledge. Students who wish to complete the Associate Certificate should submit a Program Declaration Request . About Flexible Learning Flexible Learning offers a variety of courses and programs in different delivery modes and locations to customize your learning at your own pace. You can review course prerequisites on our website and if you meet them, you’ll be able to register for that available course immediately. Some courses may require departmental approval or formal acceptance into the program. BCIT Flexible Learning courses are offered during the Winter (January), Spring/Summer (April), and Fall (September) terms. Scheduled intakes Ongoing Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) intakes: January, April, and September . Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year with intake options available during the following periods: Intake Opening (9:00 am) Deadline (11:59 pm) Winter (January) February 1st* January 2nd* Spring/Summer (April) May 1st* April 1st* Fall (September) October 1st* September 1st* *or next business day Intakes may fill before the deadline. If you are currently registered in a course or planning to start, submit your application early to secure your spot in the program. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. English language proficiency: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent Recommended for success Math: one of the following (or equivalent): Math 12* or MATH 0001 – Technical Mathematics *Students who completed Math 12 more than five years ago are strongly recommended to start with one of the required math courses. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Program declaration Declaring your Flexible Learning (Part-time Studies) program ensures that BCIT is aware of your intent to complete a program as it is currently outlined and provides you the opportunity to apply for transfer credit. To submit your declaration: Answer all questions completely. If required, convert transcripts and documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Declare Now Upon approval, a program plan letter will be sent to you confirming your program of study. Please allow approximately eight weeks for processing. Learn more about program declaration Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies
